records.source: ``(mark, note)``, the mark to draw and the sentence explaining any fallback, empty when the choice was honoured.
records.translation: ``(mark, note)``: merkið sem á að teikna og setningin sem skýrir hvaða varaleið sem er; tóm þegar valinu var fylgt.

records.context: Two vocabularies meet here and they are not the same. This module stores ``bar_jitter`` and ``box_jitter``; :class:`spacr.plot.spacrGraph` and the live panels draw ``jitter_bar`` and ``jitter_box``. A caller that reads the setting and forgets :func:`mark_for` hands matplotlib a name that ``plot.py``'s own error message lists as unknown -- which is the mistake this function exists to stop anyone making twice. Every call site that reads the setting and then draws should come through here.
records.label: spacr.graph_types.mark_to_start_on#4
records.source: TWO VOCABULARIES MEET HERE AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME. This module stores ``bar_jitter`` and ``box_jitter``; :class:`spacr.plot.spacrGraph` and the live panels draw ``jitter_bar`` and ``jitter_box``. A caller that reads the setting and forgets :func:`mark_for` hands matplotlib a name that ``plot.py``'s own error message lists as unknown -- which is the mistake this function exists to stop anyone making twice. Every call site that reads the setting and then draws should come through here.
records.translation: Hér mætast tveir orðaforðar, og þeir eru ekki þeir sömu. Þessi eining geymir ``bar_jitter`` og ``box_jitter``; :class:`spacr.plot.spacrGraph` og lifandi spjöldin teikna ``jitter_bar`` og ``jitter_box``. Kallandi sem les stillinguna og gleymir :func:`mark_for` réttir matplotlib nafn sem villuboð ``plot.py`` sjálfs telja óþekkt -- einmitt mistökin sem þetta fall er til að enginn geri tvisvar. Hver kallstaður sem les stillinguna og teiknar síðan ætti að fara hér í gegn.

records.context: The fallback is the caller's own form, not the table's default, and it is taken in MARK vocabulary because that is what a caller already has written down. A preference nobody expressed must not move an existing view, so a caller passing what it used to hardcode gets exactly that back until someone chooses otherwise.
records.label: spacr.graph_types.mark_to_start_on#5
records.source: THE FALLBACK IS THE CALLER'S OWN FORM, NOT THE TABLE'S DEFAULT, and it is taken in MARK vocabulary because that is what a caller already has written down. A preference nobody expressed must not move an existing view, so a caller passing what it used to hardcode gets exactly that back until someone chooses otherwise.
records.translation: Varaleiðin er eigið form kallandans, ekki sjálfgefið gildi töflunnar, og hún er gefin á merkjaorðaforða vegna þess að það er það sem kallandi hefur þegar skrifað niður. Val sem enginn hefur látið í ljós má ekki breyta núverandi sýn, svo kallandi sem sendir það sem hann harðkóðaði áður fær nákvæmlega það til baka þar til einhver velur annað.

records.context: The fallback is handed to :func:`start_for` UNTRANSLATED, on purpose. It looks like it needs mapping back to graph-type vocabulary first, and the first version of this function did that with a reverse lookup over :data:`MARKS`. A mutation test could not tell the two versions apart, and reading `start_for` says why: with no preference stored it answers the fallback as given, without validating it, because "a widget knows what it can draw". The reverse lookup was dead code.
records.label: spacr.graph_types.mark_to_start_on#6
records.source: THE FALLBACK IS HANDED TO :func:`start_for` UNTRANSLATED, on purpose. It looks like it needs mapping back to graph-type vocabulary first, and the first version of this function did that with a reverse lookup over :data:`MARKS`. A mutation test could not tell the two versions apart, and reading `start_for` says why: with no preference stored it answers the fallback AS GIVEN, without validating it, because "a widget knows what it can draw". The reverse lookup was dead code.
records.translation: Varaleiðin er send óþýdd til :func:`start_for`, viljandi. Það virðist sem fyrst þurfi að varpa henni aftur í orðaforða grafgerða, og fyrsta útgáfa þessa falls gerði það með öfugri uppflettingu í :data:`MARKS`. Stökkbreytingapróf gat ekki greint útgáfurnar tvær í sundur, og lestur `start_for` sýnir hvers vegna: án vistaðs vals skilar það varaleiðinni eins og hún var gefin, án þess að sannreyna hana, vegna þess að "græja veit hvað hún getur teiknað". Öfuga uppflettingin var dauður kóði.

records.context: It would stop being dead the day a caller passes ``counts``. `start_for` uses the fallback a second time on the too-thin-for-a-distribution path, where `fits(shape, fallback)` decides between the caller's form and the table default -- and a MARK spelling fails `fits`. No caller here has counts: these are settings defaults, built before any data is read. If one ever does, this function needs the mapping back and a test that reaches that path.
records.label: spacr.graph_types.mark_to_start_on#7
records.source: IT WOULD STOP BEING DEAD the day a caller passes ``counts``. `start_for` uses the fallback a second time on the too-thin-for-a-distribution path, where `fits(shape, fallback)` decides between the caller's form and the table default -- and a MARK spelling fails `fits`. No caller here has counts: these are settings defaults, built before any data is read. If one ever does, this function needs the mapping back and a test that reaches that path.
records.translation: Hún hætti að vera dauð daginn sem kallandi sendir ``counts``. `start_for` notar varaleiðina í annað sinn á leiðinni fyrir gögn sem eru of strjál fyrir dreifingu, þar sem `fits(shape, fallback)` velur milli forms kallandans og sjálfgefins gildis töflunnar -- og stafsetning á merkjaorðaforða stenst ekki `fits`. Enginn kallandi hér hefur talningar: þetta eru sjálfgefin gildi stillinga, smíðuð áður en nokkur gögn eru lesin. Ef einhver fær þær einhvern tíma þarf þetta fall öfugu vörpunina og próf sem nær þeirri leið.
